name: Vladimir Lenin
description: Leader of the 1917 Russian Revolution and founder of the Soviet Union, Lenin theorized the vanguard party, the dictatorship of the proletariat, and imperialism as the final stage of capitalism, shaping 20th-century communism.

name: Joseph Stalin
description: At the head of the Soviet Union, Stalin imposed forced industrialization, agrarian collectivization, and central planning, consolidating a single-party regime marked by purges, terror, and mass repression.

name: Mao Zedong
description: Leader of the Chinese Revolution and founder of the People's Republic, Mao adapted Marxism to the peasantry through people's war, collectivization, and the permanent mobilization of the masses in campaigns of radical transformation.

name: Leon Trotsky
description: Organizer of the Red Army, Trotsky championed permanent revolution and internationalism, becoming the main left-wing opponent of Stalinist bureaucratization until he was exiled and assassinated in Mexico.

name: Anton Pannekoek
description: A Dutch astronomer and Marxist, Pannekoek championed workers' councils and the self-organization of the masses, criticizing both reformist parliamentarism and the centralism of vanguard communist parties.

name: Kim Il-sung
description: Founder of North Korea, Kim Il-sung created the Juche doctrine of national self-reliance and established a single-party regime with a cult of the leader that fuses communism, nationalism, and hereditary dynastic power.

name: Pol Pot
description: Leader of the Khmer Rouge in Cambodia, Pol Pot imposed radical agrarian communism that emptied the cities and abolished property, causing one of the greatest genocides of the 20th century in the name of a peasant utopia.

name: Deng Xiaoping
description: The leader who reoriented China after Mao, Deng promoted market reforms and economic opening under Communist Party control, creating the model of socialism with Chinese characteristics and the country's rapid growth.

name: Ferdinand Lassalle
description: A pioneer of state socialism, Lassalle championed universal suffrage and state-funded cooperatives, founding the first major German workers' party and influencing European social democracy.

name: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk
description: Founder of modern Turkey, Atatürk imposed radical modernization from above, with secularization, a new alphabet, civil rights for women, and developmentalist nationalism, breaking with the Ottoman and religious heritage.

name: Garrett Hardin
description: An American ecologist, Hardin popularized the Tragedy of the Commons, arguing that shared resources degrade without control, a thesis that influenced debates on the environment, property, and population control.

name: Otto Neurath
description: An Austrian philosopher and economist, Neurath championed a planned economy and the technical administration of production, rejecting the market and also creating the visual language of data known as Isotype.

name: Eduard Bernstein
description: The father of Marxist revisionism, Bernstein championed a gradual, democratic transition to socialism through reforms, rejecting the inevitability of capitalist collapse and influencing modern social democracy.

name: Ernst Niekisch
description: The leading figure of German National Bolshevism, Niekisch united radical nationalism and socialist revolution against liberalism and Western influence, seeking to bring Germany closer to the East and Russia.

name: Gregor Strasser
description: Leader of the anti-capitalist wing of Nazism, Strasser championed a mass nationalist socialism with nationalizations and social reform, before being eliminated by Hitler in the Night of the Long Knives in 1934.

name: Benito Mussolini
description: The creator of fascism, Mussolini ruled Italy as a totalitarian dictatorship, fusing nationalism, a corporatist state, a cult of the leader, and expansionist militarism, serving as a model for European authoritarian regimes.

name: Adolf Hitler
description: Leader of National Socialism and the Third Reich, Hitler imposed a totalitarian, racist, expansionist regime, responsible for unleashing World War II and committing the genocide known as the Holocaust.

name: Engelbert Dollfuss
description: An Austrian chancellor, Dollfuss established Austrofascism, an authoritarian corporatist state with a Catholic base that dissolved parliament and repressed socialists and Nazis until his assassination by Nazi agents.

name: José Antonio Primo de Rivera
description: Founder of the Spanish Falange, Primo de Rivera created national syndicalism, advocating a corporatist, nationalist, Catholic state against liberalism and Marxism, becoming a martyr of the Francoist right.

name: Plínio Salgado
description: Leader of Brazilian Integralism, Plínio Salgado created an authoritarian nationalist movement of Christian inspiration, with the motto God, Fatherland and Family and mass aesthetics inspired by the European fascisms of the 1930s.

name: Lee Kuan Yew
description: Founder of Singapore, Lee Kuan Yew transformed the city-state into a model of authoritarian capitalism, uniting open markets, technocratic meritocracy, strict order, and heavily restricted political freedoms.

name: Vladimir Putin
description: Russia's leader for over 25 years, Putin crushed all real opposition, nationalized strategic sectors under patrimonial state capitalism, pushes anti-LGBT and traditional-values laws with the Orthodox Church, restricts Central Asian immigration, wages war on Ukraine, and censors the internet via AI in the name of digital sovereignty.

name: Richard Spencer
description: An American activist, Spencer popularized the term alt-right and advocates identitarian white nationalism and an ethnically homogeneous state, supremacist positions widely repudiated inside and outside the United States.

name: Steve Bannon
description: An American political strategist, Bannon articulated right-wing national populism, pitting globalist elites against an economic, cultural, and sovereigntist nationalism that influenced populist campaigns around the world.

name: Nick Land
description: A British philosopher, Land founded accelerationism and the so-called Dark Enlightenment, advocating the acceleration of capitalism and technology and criticizing egalitarian democracy in favor of new hierarchies.

name: Hendrik Verwoerd
description: Known as the architect of apartheid, Verwoerd systematized institutional racial segregation in South Africa, grounding racial nationalism in the legal and territorial separation imposed on the country's Black majority.

name: Irving Kristol
description: Considered the godfather of neoconservatism, Kristol united free markets, traditional values, and an interventionist foreign policy, shaping the American intellectual right of the second half of the 20th century.

name: Louis XIV
description: France's Sun King, Louis XIV personified monarchical absolutism by divine right, centralizing power, subjecting the nobility to the court of Versailles, and expanding the cultural and military prestige of the French kingdom.

name: António de Oliveira Salazar
description: Leader of the Portuguese Estado Novo, Salazar ran a conservative, corporatist dictatorship that united order, Catholic nationalism, and political control without mass mobilization, keeping the country isolated for decades.

name: Viktor Orbán
description: Hungary's prime minister, Orbán governs under so-called illiberal democracy, combining nationalism, Christian conservatism, sovereignty vis-à-vis the European Union, and strong control over media, courts, and institutions.

name: Benjamin Disraeli
description: A British statesman, Disraeli formulated one-nation paternalistic conservatism, reconciling tradition, monarchy, and social reforms to integrate the working classes and strengthen the country's cohesion.

name: Ruhollah Khomeini
description: Leader of the 1979 Iranian Revolution, Khomeini created the Islamic republic and instituted the rule of the religious jurist, fusing theocracy and state and transforming Iran into a revolutionary power of Shia Islam.

name: Ze'ev Jabotinsky
description: Leader of Revisionist Zionism, Jabotinsky championed an assertive Jewish nationalism, an independent military force, and a Jewish-majority state, becoming an inspiration for the contemporary Israeli right.

name: Ahad Ha'am
description: A Zionist thinker, Ahad Ha'am formulated cultural Zionism, proposing that Jewish national renewal should come first through culture, language, and ethics rather than immediate political and territorial sovereignty.

name: Curtis Yarvin
description: A political theorist known as Mencius Moldbug, Yarvin formulated neoreaction, proposing to replace democracy with a state run like a company by a sovereign-executive, on the model of neocameralism.

name: Frederick the Great
description: King of Prussia, Frederick the Great made the kingdom a military and administrative power, embodying enlightened despotism and the cameralist state of disciplined bureaucracy, centralized finances, and tolerance.

name: Joseph de Maistre
description: The leading reactionary theorist, Maistre opposed the French Revolution by defending monarchy and the authority of tradition and religion against Enlightenment rationalism, influencing European conservative thought.

name: Aleksandr Dugin
description: A Russian philosopher, Dugin formulated the Fourth Political Theory and Eurasianism, proposing a multipolar world founded on civilizations and tradition against liberalism and globalism, influencing the nationalist right.

name: Roman Dmowski
description: Founder of Polish National Democracy, Dmowski united ethnic nationalism, Catholicism, and sovereignty in a project of a homogeneous nation-state, becoming a central figure of modern Polish nationalism.

name: Leon Kass
description: An American bioethicist, Kass is the leading voice of bioconservatism, warning against genetic manipulation and human enhancement in the name of dignity, human nature, and the ethical limits of science.

name: Konrad Adenauer
description: West Germany's first chancellor, Adenauer consolidated Christian democracy, the social market economy, and the country's integration into the West, rebuilding the nation after the war and anchoring it in Europe.

name: William F. Buckley Jr.
description: An American intellectual, Buckley articulated modern conservatism in the United States, uniting free markets, anti-communism, and traditional Christian values into a coherent, influential political and cultural force.

name: Cicero
description: A Roman statesman and philosopher, Cicero defended the republic, mixed government, and the rule of law, bequeathing the tradition of civic republicanism and natural law that influenced Western political thought.

name: Montesquieu
description: A French Enlightenment philosopher, Montesquieu formulated the separation of powers and institutional moderation, defending constitutional monarchy and government limited by laws as a defense against despotism.

name: Milton Friedman
description: An American economist, Friedman led neoliberalism and monetarism, defending free markets, monetary stability, and a smaller state as essential conditions of freedom and prosperity.

name: Ludwig Erhard
description: The father of the German economic miracle, Erhard implemented the ordoliberal social market economy, uniting regulated free competition, monetary stability, and welfare, later governing as Germany's chancellor.

name: G. K. Chesterton
description: A British writer, Chesterton popularized distributism, defending the wide distribution of property and small-scale production against monopoly capitalism and state socialism, with strong Christian inspiration.

name: Henri de Saint-Simon
description: A precursor of technocracy, Saint-Simon proposed an industrial society governed by scientists, engineers, and producers instead of politicians and aristocrats, influencing later socialism and positivism.

name: Michael Sandel
description: An American political philosopher, Sandel is one of the leading exponents of communitarianism, criticizing procedural liberalism and holding that justice, virtue, and the common good arise from community bonds.

name: Adrian Wooldridge
description: A British journalist and essayist, Wooldridge is one of the leading defenders of meritocracy, arguing that selection by merit and ability drove the modern world and needs to be renewed in our time.

name: John Stuart Mill
description: A British liberal philosopher, Mill championed individual liberty, tolerance, utilitarianism, and the harm principle, making him a foundational figure of modern liberalism.

name: John Locke
description: The father of classical liberalism, Locke grounded the natural rights to life, liberty, and property and government limited by consent and the separation of powers, inspiring the modern liberal revolutions.

name: Robert Nozick
description: An American philosopher, Nozick defended libertarianism and the minimal state in Anarchy, State, and Utopia, arguing that only the protection of individual rights justifies the existence of state power.

name: Al Gore
description: A former US vice president, Al Gore became a reference of liberal environmentalism, advocating global climate action and market solutions to the ecological crisis, which earned him the Nobel Peace Prize.

name: William Beveridge
description: A British economist, Beveridge designed the United Kingdom's welfare state, proposing universal social security against poverty, disease, and unemployment as a basis for social liberalism.

name: Thomas Paine
description: A pamphleteer of the American and French revolutions, Paine defended the rights of man, the republic, and radical social reforms in popular language, spreading democratic ideals among the masses of his time.

name: Edmund Burke
description: The father of modern conservatism, Burke defended prudent reform, tradition, and institutions against abstract rationalism and revolutionary rupture, harshly criticizing the excesses of the French Revolution.

name: Friedrich Hayek
description: An Austrian economist, Hayek championed the free market and spontaneous order, warning that central planning leads to serfdom and suppresses dispersed knowledge, becoming a reference of 20th-century liberalism.

name: Gustave de Molinari
description: A Belgian economist, Molinari pioneered competitive government, proposing free competition in security and governance as an intellectual root of anarcho-capitalism and voluntary jurisdictions.

name: Henry George
description: An American economist, Henry George proposed the single tax on land value, arguing that land rent should fund society and reduce inequality rather than burdening labor or capital.

name: Charles Fourier
description: A French utopian socialist, Fourier linked social progress to the emancipation of women and criticized the patriarchal family, moral repression, and social hierarchies, imagining ideal cooperative communities.

name: Nicolas de Condorcet
description: A French Enlightenment philosopher, Condorcet championed civil rights, legal equality, and women's suffrage, linking political liberalism to universalist reforms and confidence in the progress of human reason.

name: John Rawls
description: An American philosopher, Rawls reformulated liberalism with the idea of justice as fairness, defending equal liberties and inequalities acceptable only if they benefit the least advantaged in society.

name: Aldo Leopold
description: An American conservationist, Leopold formulated the land ethic and defended a responsible relationship between human communities and soils, waters, and ecosystems, inspiring modern environmentalism.

name: Theodore Roosevelt
description: A US president, Theodore Roosevelt led the Progressive Era, fighting monopolies, regulating the market, and creating policies of environmental conservation and protection for consumers and workers.

name: Nick Srnicek
description: A Canadian political theorist, Srnicek advocates left accelerationism, proposing to use technology, automation, and basic income to move beyond work and build a post-capitalist future of shared abundance.

name: Ray Kurzweil
description: An American inventor and futurist, Kurzweil popularized transhumanism and the Singularity, predicting the fusion of humans and machines and the radical expansion of human capacities through technology.

name: Getúlio Vargas
description: A Brazilian statesman, Vargas shaped modern Brazil with developmentalist nationalism, state-directed industrialization, and labor legislation, founding Brazilian labourism and marking decades of national politics.

name: Ernest Renan
description: A French philosopher, Renan defined the nation as a daily plebiscite, founded on the will to live together and shared memory, offering the intellectual basis of civic nationalism as opposed to ethnic nationalism.

name: Evo Morales
description: Bolivia's first indigenous president, Evo Morales led indigenism and the plurinational state, nationalizing resources and expanding the rights of native peoples within a left-wing project.

name: Otto von Bismarck
description: The unifier of Germany, Bismarck created the first modern welfare state, using conservative social reforms to contain socialism and strengthen order, and steered European diplomacy for decades.

name: Mikhail Bakunin
description: A Russian revolutionary, Bakunin was the great theorist of collectivist anarchism, opposing the state and authoritarian Marxism and defending spontaneous social revolution and the free federation of communities and workers.

name: Peter Kropotkin
description: A Russian anarchist theorist, Kropotkin developed anarcho-communism and the idea of mutual aid as a factor of evolution, defending a stateless society based on cooperation, science, and free association.

name: Buenaventura Durruti
description: A Spanish anarcho-syndicalist revolutionary, Durruti was a central figure of the Spanish Revolution, leading workers' militias and collectivization during the civil war, becoming a symbol of militant anarchism.

name: Georges Sorel
description: A French theorist, Sorel developed revolutionary syndicalism and the myth of the general strike, exalting direct action and proletarian violence with influence on left and fascist movements.

name: Noam Chomsky
description: An American linguist and thinker, Chomsky revolutionized linguistics and became an influential voice of libertarian socialism, criticizing corporate power, the media, and US imperialism in the world.

name: Antonio Gramsci
description: An Italian Marxist theorist, Gramsci developed the concept of cultural hegemony, showing how ruling classes govern through consent, and championed cultural struggle as the path to social transformation.

name: Josip Broz Tito
description: Leader of socialist Yugoslavia, Tito unified diverse peoples under a single party, adopted workers' self-management, and broke with Moscow, leading the Non-Aligned Movement during the Cold War.

name: Oskar Lange
description: A Polish economist, Lange championed market socialism, arguing that planning could simulate prices and allocate resources efficiently, in the famous socialist calculation debate.

name: Pierre-Joseph Proudhon
description: A French philosopher, Proudhon was the first to declare himself an anarchist and formulated mutualism, defending fair exchange, free credit, and use-based property, with the famous phrase that property is theft.

name: Abdullah Öcalan
description: A Kurdish political leader, Öcalan abandoned revolutionary Marxism and formulated democratic confederalism, inspiring the autonomous experiment of Rojava, based on self-management, ecology, and gender equality.

name: Benjamin Tucker
description: An American individualist anarchist, Tucker championed a free market without state or monopolies, uniting radical individual freedom and mutualism, and translated the great libertarian thinkers of his time.

name: Murray Bookchin
description: An American thinker, Bookchin created social ecology and communalism, defending autonomous municipalities, direct democracy, and harmony with nature, influencing radical environmentalism and the Rojava experiment.

name: Keir Hardie
description: A Scottish politician, Keir Hardie was a founder of the British Labour Party, defending workers' rights, suffrage, and social reforms within democracy, marking the birth of modern labourism.

name: Jacques Maritain
description: A French Catholic philosopher, Maritain renewed Christian thought and influenced Christian democracy, defending human rights, integral humanism, and the compatibility of faith, reason, and democratic freedom.

name: Martin Buber
description: An Austrian Jewish philosopher, Buber developed the philosophy of dialogue, summed up in the I–Thou relationship, and championed a communitarian, humanist socialism, influencing religious thought and cultural Zionism.

name: Olof Palme
description: A Swedish statesman, Olof Palme was one of the greatest names of social democracy, expanding the welfare state and championing disarmament, international solidarity, and the rights of poorer countries.

name: Karl Marx
description: A German philosopher and economist, Marx created historical materialism and the critique of capitalism, analyzing class struggle and the exploitation of labor, and became the greatest reference of socialism and communism.

name: Carlo Rosselli
description: An Italian antifascist thinker, Rosselli formulated liberal socialism, seeking to unite liberalism's ideals of freedom with socialism's social justice, and organized the resistance against Mussolini's regime.

name: George Orwell
description: A British writer, Orwell was a democratic socialist and fierce critic of totalitarianism, denouncing in works such as 1984 and Animal Farm authoritarianism, the manipulation of truth, and the oppression of power.

name: André Gorz
description: An Austro-French philosopher, Gorz was a pioneer of political ecology and post-Marxism, criticizing productivism and wage labor and defending shorter working hours and basic income in a freer society.

name: Arne Næss
description: A Norwegian philosopher, Næss founded deep ecology, defending the intrinsic value of all life and a radical change of values to reduce human impact and restore harmony between people and nature.

name: Emiliano Zapata
description: A Mexican revolutionary, Zapata led peasants in the Mexican Revolution under the motto Land and Liberty, defending agrarian reform and the autonomy of rural communities against large landowners and the state.

name: Émile Armand
description: A French individualist anarchist, Émile Armand championed the absolute sovereignty of the individual, a life free of moral and state impositions, and free association, influencing egoist anarchism and the counterculture.

name: Daniel Guérin
description: A French libertarian socialist, Guérin sought to unite Marxism and anarchism, defending workers' self-management and sexual liberation, and was an important historian of revolutions and the labor movement.

name: Leo Tolstoy
description: A Russian writer, Tolstoy united his literary work with pacifist Christian anarchism, preaching nonviolence, simplicity, and refusal of the state in ways that influenced Gandhi and later movements.

name: Henry David Thoreau
description: An American writer, Thoreau championed civil disobedience, simple living in contact with nature, and the right to resist unjust laws, influencing pacifists and environmentalists.

name: John Zerzan
description: An American philosopher, Zerzan is one of the leading voices of anarcho-primitivism, criticizing civilization, technology, and domestication as sources of oppression and defending a return to ancestral ways of life.

name: Max Stirner
description: A German philosopher, Stirner is the great reference of egoist anarchism, rejecting state, morality, and institutions as oppressive abstractions and placing the sovereign individual and their interests at the center of everything.

name: Murray Rothbard
description: An American economist, Rothbard was the main formulator of anarcho-capitalism, defending the abolition of the state, absolute private property, and the provision of security and justice by the free market.

name: Frédéric Bastiat
description: A French economist, Bastiat defended free trade and limited government with clarity and irony, denouncing protectionism and what is not seen in economic policies, becoming a classic of liberal thought.

name: Ludwig von Mises
description: An Austrian economist, Mises was a great defender of the free market and demonstrated the impossibility of rational economic calculation under socialism, becoming a pillar of the Austrian School and an inspiration for modern libertarianism.

name: Ron Paul
description: An American politician, Ron Paul popularized libertarianism in the United States, defending the minimal state, individual freedom, sound money, and a non-interventionist foreign policy against the establishment.

name: Hans-Hermann Hoppe
description: A German economist, Hoppe radicalized anarcho-capitalism, defending absolute private property and criticizing democracy as a system that erodes freedom, proposing social orders based on voluntary contract.

name: Adam Smith
description: A Scottish economist, Adam Smith founded modern economics in The Wealth of Nations, showing how the market and the division of labor generate prosperity and how the invisible hand coordinates individual interests.

name: Leonard Peikoff
description: An Objectivist philosopher, Peikoff was Ayn Rand's principal intellectual heir, systematizing Objectivism and defending reason, individualism, and laissez-faire capitalism as the foundations of life and morality.

name: Elon Musk
description: An entrepreneur and billionaire, Musk leads technology companies such as Tesla and SpaceX and champions technological accelerationism, the colonization of Mars, and libertarian ideas, influencing the global public debate.

name: Roger Scruton
description: A British philosopher, Scruton was one of the great contemporary conservative thinkers, defending tradition, beauty, nation, and institutions as sources of meaning and order against relativism and progressivism.

name: Friedrich List
description: A German economist, List championed economic nationalism and the protection of infant industry, arguing that lagging countries need tariffs and a strong state to develop and catch up with rich nations.

name: Samuel Edward Konkin III
description: An American libertarian theorist, Konkin created agorism, advocating the replacement of the state through free, parallel markets and counter-economics, using informal activity to erode state power.

name: Phil Zimmermann
description: An American cryptographer, Zimmermann created PGP, making strong cryptography accessible to everyone and defending digital privacy as a right, becoming a reference for crypto-anarchism and civil liberties.

name: Max More
description: A British philosopher, Max More is one of the founders of modern transhumanism and extropianism, defending the use of technology to overcome human limits, extend life, and expand individual freedom.

name: Javier Milei
description: An Argentine statesman and economist, Milei champions anarcho-capitalism and radical liberalism, proposing to drastically cut the state, dollarize the economy, and fight inflation, reaching Argentina's presidency.

name: Otto von Habsburg
description: An Austrian politician and heir of the Habsburgs, Otto was a defender of constitutional monarchy, European federalism, and continental integration, serving for decades as a European parliamentarian and critic of totalitarianism.

name: Barry Goldwater
description: An American politician, Goldwater was a decisive figure of the modern right in the United States, defending free markets, anti-communism, and limited government, and paving the way for Reaganite conservatism.

name: Ezra Heywood
description: An American individualist anarchist, Heywood championed a free market without monopolies, the abolition of the state, and the emancipation of women, uniting radical economic freedom with the fight for sexual and civil liberty.

name: Randolph Bourne
description: An American essayist, Bourne sharply criticized militarism and nationalism, coining the idea that war is the health of the state, and championed a cultural cosmopolitanism open to diversity and freedom.

name: Peter Maurin
description: A French Christian activist, Maurin co-founded the Catholic Worker Movement, defending social justice, voluntary poverty, and communities of work and mutual aid inspired by the social doctrine of the Church.

name: Lysander Spooner
description: An American jurist and anarchist, Spooner championed natural law and the free market, questioned the legitimacy of the Constitution and the state, and challenged public monopolies, influencing libertarianism.

name: Emmanuel Macron
description: A French statesman, Macron reached France's presidency as a centrist, liberal reformer, defending markets, European integration, and economic reforms, seeking to overcome the traditional divide between left and right.

name: Auguste Comte
description: A French philosopher, Comte founded positivism and sociology, holding that science should organize society toward order and progress, with strong influence on republican and technocratic thought.

name: Tomáš Garrigue Masaryk
description: A Czech statesman and philosopher, Masaryk was the founder and first president of Czechoslovakia, defending humanist democracy, minority rights, and ethical values as the basis of national political life.

name: Leonardo Boff
description: A Brazilian theologian, Boff is one of the leading names of Liberation Theology, uniting Christian faith with the struggle for social justice and the defense of the poor and the environment, with strong criticism of capitalism and inequality.

name: Park Chung-hee
description: A South Korean dictator, Park Chung-hee led an authoritarian developmentalist regime that rapidly industrialized South Korea through state planning and discipline, turning the country into an economic power.

name: Henry Kissinger
description: An American diplomat, Kissinger was a master of realpolitik, shaping US foreign policy in the Cold War with détente, the opening to China, and controversial interventions in the name of the national interest.

name: Paul Romer
description: An American economist, Romer is a reference of endogenous growth theory, showing how ideas, innovation, and knowledge drive development, and proposed charter cities as an institutional reform.

name: Peter Thiel
description: An American entrepreneur and investor, Thiel is an influential figure of tech capitalism and champions libertarian and neoreactionary ideas, skeptical of democracy and enthusiastic about disruptive innovation.

name: Salvador Allende
description: A Chilean statesman, Allende was the first democratically elected Marxist president in Latin America, seeking to build socialism by peaceful means until he was overthrown by Pinochet's military coup in 1973.

name: Filippo Tommaso Marinetti
description: An Italian poet, Marinetti founded futurism, exalting speed, the machine, war, and the break with the past, and drew close to fascism, uniting artistic avant-garde and revolutionary nationalism.

name: Donald Trump
description: An entrepreneur and US president, Trump leads the nationalist populism of the MAGA movement, with tariff protectionism, restrictive immigration policy, and anti-establishment rhetoric that redefined the right.

name: Xi Jinping
description: China's leader, Xi Jinping concentrated power like no successor of Mao, reinforcing the Communist Party's control, nationalism, and the country's global projection through technology and economic influence.

name: Lula da Silva
description: A Brazilian statesman, Lula rose from union activism to Brazil's presidency, leading the left with social programs, anti-poverty policies, and a development project with a strong state presence.

name: Nayib Bukele
description: El Salvador's president, Bukele gained prominence for his tough security policy against gangs and the adoption of bitcoin, uniting strong popular support, digital communication, and growing concentration of power.

name: Volodymyr Zelensky
description: Ukraine's president, Zelensky went from actor to statesman and became a symbol of national resistance to the Russian invasion, defending democracy, sovereignty, and his country's rapprochement with the West.

name: Bernie Sanders
description: An American politician, Bernie Sanders is the leading voice of democratic socialism in the United States, defending universal public healthcare, labor rights, and the fight against inequality and the power of large corporations.

name: Mohammed bin Salman
description: Saudi Arabia's crown prince, Mohammed bin Salman concentrates power and conducts a controlled economic and social modernization, diversifying the oil economy while maintaining strong political repression.

name: Mahatma Gandhi
description: Leader of India's independence, Gandhi developed nonviolent resistance and civil disobedience against British rule, becoming a world symbol of the peaceful struggle for freedom and social justice.

name: B. R. Ambedkar
description: An Indian jurist and reformer, Ambedkar was the principal architect of India's Constitution and leader of the Dalits, fighting the caste system and defending rights, equality, and social justice for the oppressed.

name: Frantz Fanon
description: A Martinican psychiatrist and theorist, Fanon was a great anti-colonial thinker, analyzing the psychological effects of racism and colonization and defending the liberation of oppressed peoples from imperial rule.

name: Thomas Sankara
description: A revolutionary from Burkina Faso, Sankara led a Marxist, pan-Africanist government that promoted self-sufficiency, women's rights, and radical social reforms, becoming an anti-imperialist icon of Africa.

name: Nelson Mandela
description: A South African statesman, Mandela led the struggle against apartheid, spent decades in prison, and became the country's first Black president, a world symbol of reconciliation, democracy, and human rights.

name: Malcolm X
description: An American activist, Malcolm X was a radical voice of the Black struggle in the United States, defending pride, self-defense, and African-American emancipation, evolving toward a more universalist vision before his assassination.

name: Sayyid Qutb
description: An Egyptian theorist, Qutb was one of the main ideologues of modern Islamism, advocating a return to Islamic law and the rejection of Western influence, becoming a reference for fundamentalist movements.

name: Carl Schmitt
description: A German jurist, Schmitt was an influential and controversial theorist of power, defining politics by the friend-enemy distinction and defending sovereignty and the state of exception.

name: Confucius
description: An ancient Chinese philosopher, Confucius created an ethic based on virtue, social harmony, and respect for hierarchies and traditions, shaping Chinese culture, morality, and politics for millennia.

name: Sun Yat-sen
description: A Chinese statesman, Sun Yat-sen led the revolution that overthrew the empire and founded the Republic of China, formulating the Three Principles of the People, uniting nationalism, democracy, and the people's welfare.

name: Theodor Herzl
description: An Austro-Hungarian journalist, Herzl was the founder of modern political Zionism, advocating the creation of a Jewish national state as a response to antisemitism, becoming a central figure in Israel's history.

name: Hugo Chávez
description: A Venezuelan statesman, Chávez led 21st-century socialism, nationalizing sectors, funding social programs with oil, and concentrating power in a Bolivarian project of strong popular and nationalist appeal.

name: Simón Bolívar
description: A South American military leader, Bolívar was the great liberator who led the independence of several countries of Spanish America, dreaming of uniting the continent under strong, centralized republics.

name: Julius Evola
description: An Italian philosopher, Evola was a traditionalist theorist of the radical right, defending hierarchy, spirituality, and the refusal of the modern world, becoming a reference of 20th-century reactionary and esoteric thought.

name: Slavoj Žižek
description: A Slovenian philosopher, Žižek unites Marxism, psychoanalysis, and cultural criticism to analyze ideology and contemporary capitalism, becoming one of the most popular and provocative left-wing thinkers of our time.

name: Isaiah Berlin
description: A British philosopher, Berlin distinguished negative from positive liberty and championed value pluralism, warning against totalitarian utopias and becoming a reference of 20th-century liberal thought.

name: Karl Liebknecht
description: A German revolutionary, Liebknecht was a socialist leader and co-founder of the Spartacus League, opposing World War I and leading the failed 1919 uprising, being murdered alongside Rosa Luxemburg.

name: Nathaniel Branden
description: An Objectivist psychologist, Branden was Ayn Rand's collaborator and a pioneer of the psychology of self-esteem, uniting Objectivism with the appreciation of reason, individualism, and personal responsibility in mental life.

name: Jean-Paul Sartre
description: A French philosopher, Sartre was the great name of existentialism, defending the radical freedom and responsibility of the individual, and drew close to Marxism, engaging in the great political causes of his time.

name: José Bové
description: A French activist, José Bové became a symbol of the anti-globalization movement and peasant agriculture, defending food sovereignty, ecology, and resistance to multinationals and genetically modified food.

name: Matteo Salvini
description: An Italian politician, Salvini leads Italy's nationalist right, championing the fight against immigration, national sovereignty, and skepticism toward the European Union, with strong populist and identitarian appeal.

name: Jeremy Corbyn
description: A British politician, Corbyn led the socialist wing of the Labour Party, defending the nationalization of services, the welfare state, anti-imperialism, and policies of strong income redistribution.

name: Ciro Gomes
description: A Brazilian politician, Ciro Gomes champions a national-developmentalist project, with a strong state role in the economy, industrialization, and national sovereignty, positioning himself as a voice of center-left labourism.

name: Jair Bolsonaro
description: A Brazilian politician, Bolsonaro reached the presidency leading the nationalist, conservative right, with agendas of security, traditional values, economic liberalism, and strong anti-establishment rhetoric.

name: Michel Temer
description: A Brazilian statesman, Temer assumed Brazil's presidency after Dilma's impeachment, conducting a liberal agenda of economic reforms and fiscal adjustment with the support of the political center and the business community.

name: Fernando Henrique Cardoso
description: A Brazilian sociologist and statesman, Fernando Henrique stabilized the economy with the Real Plan and, as president, conducted liberal reforms, privatizations, and the modernization of the state within social democracy.

name: Emílio Garrastazu Médici
description: A Brazilian general and dictator, Médici governed during the most repressive period of the military dictatorship, uniting heavy censorship and political persecution with the so-called economic miracle of accelerated growth and colossal public works.

name: Humberto Castelo Branco
description: A Brazilian military officer and statesman, Castelo Branco was the first president of the military dictatorship begun in 1964, conducting the initial repression and economic reforms of liberal orientation and alignment with the United States.

name: João Goulart
description: A Brazilian statesman, João Goulart was a reformist left-wing president, a defender of grassroots reforms and workers' rights, deposed by the 1964 military coup that began the dictatorship in Brazil.

name: Leonel Brizola
description: A Brazilian politician, Brizola was one of the great names of labourism, defending nationalism, social reforms, public education, and workers' rights, with strong activity before and after the dictatorship.

name: Francisco Franco
description: A Spanish general and dictator, Franco won the Civil War and ruled for decades over a nationalist, Catholic, authoritarian regime, repressing opponents and preserving a corporatist order until his death.

name: Barack Obama
description: An American statesman, Obama symbolized moderate progressive liberalism, expanding public healthcare, civil rights, and multilateral diplomacy within an institutional market economy.

name: Benjamin Netanyahu
description: An Israeli politician, Netanyahu became a central figure of Israel's nationalist, security-focused right, uniting economic liberalism, conservative Zionism, and a hard line against regional adversaries.

name: Augusto Pinochet
description: A Chilean general and dictator, Pinochet overthrew Allende and established an anti-communist military regime, combining political repression, authoritarian conservatism, and neoliberal reforms.

name: Fidel Castro
description: A Cuban revolutionary, Fidel Castro led the 1959 revolution and built a single-party socialist state, anti-imperialist and nationalist, with a state-run economy and strong repression.

name: José Mujica
description: A former guerrilla and Uruguayan statesman, Mujica embodied a democratic left, austere and libertarian in customs, defending moderate redistribution, civil rights, and a critique of consumerism.

name: Recep Tayyip Erdoğan
description: A Turkish statesman, Erdoğan shifted Turkey toward Islamic, nationalist conservatism, combining presidential centralization, an assertive foreign policy, and the erosion of democratic checks.

name: Bashar al-Assad
description: A Syrian dictator, Bashar al-Assad preserved the Baathist regime through the military apparatus, repression, and Russian-Iranian support during the civil war, until being overthrown in 2024 and departing into exile.

name: John F. Kennedy
description: An American statesman, Kennedy combined reformist liberalism, Cold War anti-communism, civil rights, and technological modernization, symbolizing the New Frontier agenda.

name: Ronald Reagan
description: An American statesman, Reagan led the modern conservative right, championing tax cuts, free markets, traditional values, firm anti-communism, and expanded military power.

name: George W. Bush
description: An American statesman, George W. Bush united religious conservatism, tax cuts, and a neoconservative foreign policy, marked by the War on Terror and the invasions of Afghanistan and Iraq.

name: Joe Biden
description: An American statesman, Biden represents the liberal Democratic center, combining a moderate welfare state, international alliances, institutional defense, and gradual progressive advances.

name: John McAfee
description: A programmer and entrepreneur, McAfee became a radical libertarian voice, defending privacy, cryptocurrencies, individual freedom, and deep distrust of the state, taxes, and government surveillance.

name: Hal Finney
description: A cryptographer and cypherpunk pioneer, Finney created reusable proof-of-work, received the first Bitcoin transaction, and championed digital privacy, decentralization, and technical freedom.

name: Kim Jong Un
description: The North Korean dictator, Kim Jong Un preserved the dynastic Juche regime, with single-party rule, a cult of the leader, nuclear militarization, a state economy, and rigid isolation from the outside world.

name: George Washington
description: Founder and first president of the United States, Washington combined military leadership, constitutional republicanism, federalism, and diplomatic prudence, defending a strong republic without permanent entanglement in foreign alliances.

name: Benjamin Franklin
description: A polymath, diplomat, and founder of the United States, Franklin united republicanism, free thought, commerce, science, innovation, and institutional pragmatism, symbolizing a liberal, cosmopolitan, Enlightenment strand of modern politics.

name: Abraham Lincoln
description: US president during the Civil War, Lincoln preserved the Union, strengthened the federal government, and led the abolition of slavery, combining civic nationalism, democratic republicanism, and progressive moral reform.

name: Alex Karp
description: An American entrepreneur, Karp leads Palantir and symbolizes a security-focused technocracy that brings together state, defense, data, and artificial intelligence, defending strategic technology in the service of Western democracies.

name: James Madison
description: A founder of the United States and principal architect of the Constitution, Madison championed federalism, the separation of powers, and individual rights, seeking to balance strong republican government with checks against tyranny.

name: Alexander Hamilton
description: A founder of the United States, Hamilton championed strong federal government, robust public finances, a national bank, and industrialization, combining constitutional republicanism with modernizing economic nationalism.

name: Maximilien Robespierre
description: A central figure of the French Revolution, Robespierre linked republican virtue, popular sovereignty, and civil equality to a centralized revolutionary power, becoming a symbol of Jacobinism and the Terror.

name: Alexander the Great
description: King of Macedon and conqueror of Persia, Alexander combined military monarchy, imperial expansion, city founding, and the integration of Greek, Macedonian, and Eastern elites after defeating the Achaemenids.

name: Napoleon Bonaparte
description: A French general and emperor, Napoleon consolidated the Revolution's administrative and legal reforms while concentrating personal power, expanding France militarily and shaping European modernizing authoritarianism.

name: Julius Caesar
description: A Roman general and statesman, Caesar combined military prestige, popular reforms, and the concentration of personal authority, weakening the aristocratic republic and paving the way for imperial power in Rome.

name: Caesar Augustus
description: The first Roman emperor, Augustus turned the republican crisis into a stable imperial order, preserving institutional forms while centralizing military command, administration, and political authority.

name: Charlemagne
description: King of the Franks and emperor, Charlemagne united military expansion, Christianization, administrative reform, and cultural patronage, becoming a symbol of imperial Christian monarchy and the medieval European order.

name: Enéas Carneiro
description: A Brazilian physician and politician, Enéas championed economic nationalism, technological sovereignty, nuclear energy, strong armed forces, and state planning, becoming a popular symbol of national developmentalism.

name: Jordan Peterson
description: A Canadian psychologist, Peterson became a reference of liberal cultural conservatism, criticizing identity progressivism and defending individual responsibility, tradition, free speech, and symbolic order.

name: Aristotle
description: A Greek philosopher, Aristotle formulated a political vision centered on the polis, civic virtue, and mixed government, defending moderate private property, natural hierarchy, and moral education as the foundations of common life.

name: Plato
description: A Greek philosopher, Plato criticized Athenian democracy and imagined a city governed by philosophers, with rigid education, moral censorship, and the strong subordination of private interests to the harmony of the political community.

name: Michel Foucault
description: A French philosopher, Foucault analyzed prisons, sexuality, medicine, and modern knowledge as forms of disciplinary power, becoming a reference for critiques of social normalization, institutions of control, and cultural hierarchies.

name: Alexis de Tocqueville
description: A French liberal thinker, Tocqueville studied American democracy and championed civil associations, decentralization, and political freedom as antidotes to the tyranny of the majority and the administrative centralization of the modern state.

name: Friedrich Nietzsche
description: A German philosopher, Nietzsche attacked egalitarian morality, Christianity, and modern resentment, defending the aristocratic creation of values, the affirmation of life, and the overcoming of inherited moral conventions.

name: Jean-Jacques Rousseau
description: An Enlightenment philosopher, Rousseau criticized social inequality and championed popular sovereignty, the general will, and a republican political community capable of forming free citizens through civic education and public virtue.

name: Thomas Hobbes
description: An English philosopher, Hobbes founded a contractualist theory of the sovereign state, defending strong central authority to contain civil war, guarantee security, and subordinate religious and factional conflicts to public peace.

name: Niccolò Machiavelli
description: A Florentine diplomat and thinker, Machiavelli analyzed political power realistically, valuing virtù, one's own military force, reason of state, and republican institutions capable of preserving liberty and civic greatness.

name: John Maynard Keynes
description: A British economist, Keynes formulated modern macroeconomics and championed the use of fiscal policy, public investment, and demand management to stabilize liberal capitalism without abolishing private property.

name: Pedro I of Brazil
description: Brazil's first emperor, Pedro I led independence and established a centralized constitutional monarchy, reconciling dynastic liberalism, personal authority, territorial unity, and the defense of the imperial order.

name: Pedro II of Brazil
description: Brazil's second emperor, Pedro II governed as a constitutional monarch, valuing parliamentarism, institutional stability, science, education, and gradual abolition, preserving national unity under the moderating power.

name: Juan Domingo Perón
description: An Argentine president and founder of Peronism, Perón combined popular nationalism, labor rights, corporatism, protected industrialization, charismatic leadership, and a third position between liberalism and communism.

name: Franklin D. Roosevelt
description: US president during the Great Depression and World War II, Roosevelt created the New Deal, expanding regulation, social rights, and federal intervention to save liberal democracy and reformed capitalism.

name: Satoshi Nakamoto
description: The pseudonym of Bitcoin's creator, Satoshi Nakamoto formulated a peer-to-peer digital currency based on cryptographic proof, decentralization, programmed scarcity, and relative privacy, without depending on banks, governments, or intermediaries.

name: George Soros
description: An investor and founder of the Open Society Foundations, Soros defends liberal democracy, human rights, civil society, multiculturalism, drug policy reform, secularism, and open institutions against authoritarianism and closed nationalism.

name: Bill Gates
description: Co-founder of Microsoft and leader of the Gates Foundation, Gates combines technological capitalism, global philanthropy, public health, education, the fight against poverty, climate innovation, and trust in science, metrics, and technocratic solutions.

name: Dalai Lama (Tenzin Gyatso)
description: The spiritual leader of Tibetan Buddhism, the 14th Dalai Lama champions nonviolence, Tibetan autonomy through the middle way, democratization of the exiled community, and dialogue between science and religion.

name: Pentti Linkola
description: A Finnish fisherman and thinker, Linkola advocated an anti-democratic, anti-technological deep ecology, with a strong state, an end to economic growth, and a drastic reduction of population to save the biosphere, becoming a reference of eco-authoritarianism.

name: Thomas Jefferson
description: Author of the Declaration of Independence and third US president, Jefferson championed an agrarian republic of small landowners, limited and decentralized government, religious freedom, and distrust of banks, armies, and cities.

name: János Kádár
description: Hungary's leader after the 1956 Soviet repression, Kádár consolidated pragmatic communism, single-party rule, alignment with Moscow, and limited economic opening aimed at consumption.

name: H. L. Mencken
description: A scathing critic of American democracy, Mencken combined economic libertarianism, Nietzschean elitism, and militant atheism, attacking puritanism, mass culture, and popular faith in newspapers and essays.

name: Marcus Garvey
description: Founder of the largest Black mass movement in history, Garvey preached Black nationalism, racial pride, entrepreneurship as a path to emancipation, and the return to Africa, rejecting integration in favor of separation and self-reliance.

name: Julius Nyerere
description: The father of Tanzania's independence, Nyerere created Ujamaa, an African socialism based on communal villages, self-reliance, and national unity above ethnicity.

name: Pope Pius IX
role: Pope and monarch of the Papal States
description: The last Pope-King, Pius IX ruled the Papal States until 1870 in the longest pontificate in history, defined the dogma of the Immaculate Conception, proclaimed papal infallibility at Vatican I, and condemned liberalism in the Syllabus of Errors.

name: Justinian I
description: Emperor of the Byzantine Empire at its height, Justinian I codified Roman law in the Corpus Juris Civilis, reconquered Italy, North Africa, and southern Spain, ordered the construction of Hagia Sophia, and imposed Chalcedonian orthodoxy.

name: Philip II of Spain
role: King of Spain and global emperor
description: Philip II ruled the largest empire of his age, defending the Counter-Reformation, financing the Inquisition, confronting England, and centralizing the Spanish monarchy at El Escorial.

name: Peter the Great
description: Tsar of Russia from 1682 to 1725, Peter I forcibly modernized the Russian Empire, Europeanizing the nobility, creating a navy, and subordinating the Orthodox Church to the state.

name: John Calvin
description: A French theologian and the main reformer of the Calvinist tradition, author of the Institutes of the Christian Religion, he organized Geneva as a theocratic republic between 1541 and 1564, disciplining public morality and creating the Puritan model.

name: Manuel I of Portugal
description: Manuel I reigned at the height of Portuguese maritime expansion, when Vasco da Gama reached India and Cabral reached Brazil, centralizing the spice trade through the Casa da India.

name: Genghis Khan
description: Born Temujin, Genghis Khan unified the Mongol tribes in 1206, reorganized steppe society into a meritocratic military machine, and launched conquests that devastated rival empires while opening routes of trade, exchange, and pragmatic religious tolerance.

name: Lázaro Cárdenas
description: Revolutionary general and president of Mexico, Cárdenas nationalized oil, expanded the ejidos, incorporated workers and peasants into the state, and consolidated post-revolutionary secular national populism.

name: Guillaume Faye
description: A philosopher and activist of the French New Right, Faye coined the concept of archeofuturism, arguing for a fusion of archaic tradition, ethnic identity, and hyper-modern technology in the face of an approaching civilizational collapse.

name: Juscelino Kubitschek
description: President of Brazil (1956–1961), Kubitschek launched the Target Plan and the construction of Brasília under the slogan "fifty years in five," promoting rapid industrialization, foreign borrowing, and developmentalist optimism.

name: José Bonifácio
description: A scientist and statesman known as the "Patriarch of Independence," José Bonifácio was the chief political architect of Brazil's 1822 separation from Portugal, favoring a centralized state, gradual abolition of slavery, and a unified nation under constitutional monarchy.

name: Zumbi dos Palmares
description: The last great leader of Palmares, the largest settlement of escaped slaves in the Americas, Zumbi resisted colonial expeditions for decades in defense of freedom for thousands of enslaved Africans and their descendants, becoming a foremost symbol of anti-slavery resistance.

name: Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca
description: An army marshal who led the proclamation of the republic in 1889, Deodoro da Fonseca became the country's first president, ruling in a centralizing and authoritarian manner until dissolving Congress in 1891, resigning shortly after amid institutional crisis.

name: Ernesto Geisel
description: A general and president during the military regime, Geisel pursued a policy of "slow, gradual, and safe" political opening, combining controlled liberalization with selective repression of opponents and strong state intervention in the economy.

name: Justin Trudeau
description: Prime Minister of Canada (2015–2025) for the Liberal Party, Trudeau promoted multiculturalism, welcoming immigrants and refugees, progressive gender and environmental policies, and a centrist governing style backed by strong state social intervention.

name: Muammar Gaddafi
description: Leader of Libya for over four decades after the 1969 coup, Gaddafi established a "Jamahiriya" of theoretical direct democracy under de facto authoritarian control, nationalized oil, funded pan-Africanist and third-worldist movements, and was deposed and killed during the 2011 civil war.

name: Lee Teng-hui
description: President of Taiwan (1988–2000) and the first directly elected by popular vote, Lee guided the transition from Kuomintang one-party rule to a full multiparty democracy, promoting a distinct Taiwanese identity and economic liberalization.

name: Chiang Kai-shek
description: Leader of the Kuomintang and the Republic of China, Chiang led the fight against the communists and the Japanese occupation, and after the 1949 defeat established a nationalist one-party regime and martial law in Taiwan, combining militant anti-communism with authoritarian developmentalism.

name: Hirohito
description: Emperor of Japan from 1926 to 1989, Hirohito reigned during militarist expansion and World War II as a figure of divine authority within the imperial system, and after defeat renounced his divine status and presided as a symbolic constitutional monarch over the country's democratic reconstruction.

name: Winston Churchill
description: British prime minister who led the United Kingdom against Nazi Germany in World War II, Churchill combined staunch defense of the British Empire and liberal capitalism with fervent anti-communist rhetoric, and was also the author of controversial colonial and wartime decisions.

name: Franz Ferdinand
description: Heir apparent to the Austro-Hungarian throne, Franz Ferdinand favored a trialist federalism to accommodate the empire's Slavic nationalities and ease internal tensions; his 1914 assassination in Sarajevo triggered World War I.

name: Woodrow Wilson
description: President of the United States (1913–1921), Wilson pursued progressive domestic reforms, led the country into World War I in the name of liberal democracy, and championed national self-determination and the creation of the League of Nations, despite maintaining segregationist policies at home.

name: Nicholas II
description: The last Tsar of Russia, Nicholas II ruled as an autocrat reluctant to cede power, led the country to defeat in World War I amid economic and social crisis, and was deposed and executed by the Bolsheviks in 1918 following the Russian Revolution.

name: Ted Kaczynski
description: A former mathematics professor who withdrew to a remote cabin in Montana and carried out a nationwide bombing campaign for nearly two decades against scientists and executives, Kaczynski argued in his manifesto 'Industrial Society and Its Future' that industrial technology destroys human freedom and must be reversed through deliberate collapse.

name: Bill Clinton
description: President of the United States (1993–2001), Clinton promoted a 'Third Way' combining fiscal discipline and welfare reform with investment in education and technology, liberalized trade through NAFTA and China's WTO accession, and oversaw a period of strong economic growth despite being impeached over a personal scandal.

name: Harry S. Truman
description: President of the United States (1945–1953), Truman ordered the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, launched the Marshall Plan and the containment doctrine at the outset of the Cold War, racially integrated the armed forces, and led the United States into the Korean War.

name: Dwight D. Eisenhower
description: Supreme commander of Allied forces in World War II and later President of the United States (1953–1961), Eisenhower expanded the interstate highway system, pursued containment of communism through diplomatic and intelligence means, and warned in his farewell address against the power of the 'military-industrial complex.'

name: Napoleon III
description: Nephew of Napoleon Bonaparte, elected president of the French Second Republic and later self-proclaimed emperor in 1852, Napoleon III modernized Paris through Haussmann's urban renewal, promoted industrialization and free trade, but led France into disaster in the Franco-Prussian War of 1870, which ended his reign.

name: Pope Francis
description: The first Jesuit and Latin American pope, Francis championed migrants and the poor, criticized unregulated capitalism and the 'throwaway culture' in his encyclical Laudato Si' on the environmental crisis, and promoted greater pastoral decentralization and open dialogue within the Catholic Church.

name: Pope Leo XIV
description: The first pope born in the United States, elected in 2025 after decades of missionary work in Peru, Leo XIV chose his name in reference to Leo XIII and his social doctrine on workers' rights, champions migrants, and warns of the risks artificial intelligence poses to human dignity and labor.

name: Thomas Aquinas
description: A Dominican friar and the foremost systematizer of medieval scholasticism, Thomas Aquinas fused Aristotelian philosophy with Christian theology in the Summa Theologica, arguing for natural law as the basis of moral and political order, the authority of the Church and the Christian monarch, and hierarchy as the earthly reflection of divine order.

name: Charles Darwin
description: A British naturalist who formulated the theory of evolution by natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species,' Darwin revolutionized the scientific understanding of life, championed empirical observation and gradualism against established dogma, and his ideas were later appropriated (in distorted form) by social ideologies he himself did not endorse.

name: Renan Santos
description: A Brazilian businessman and political activist, he founded the Free Brazil Movement (MBL) in 2014 and has chaired the Mission party since 2025 on a platform he sums up as 'Milei in form, Bukele in substance,' running for the Brazilian presidency in 2026.

name: Flávio Bolsonaro
description: A senator from Rio de Janeiro and the eldest son of Jair Bolsonaro, he is the Liberal Party's pre-candidate for the presidency in 2026; he made public security his main banner in the Senate and backs selective privatizations and cuts to public spending.

name: Anders Fogh Rasmussen
description: Liberal Prime Minister of Denmark (2001–2009) and later Secretary General of NATO (2009–2014), Rasmussen combined market reforms with the Nordic welfare state, championing free trade, European integration, and secular, progressive values.

name: Zohran Mamdani
description: Mayor of New York City and Uganda-born democratic socialist, Mamdani champions rent freezes, city-owned grocery stores, free buses, and sanctuary-city protections for immigrants, while moderating in office by keeping the police commissioner in place.

name: JD Vance
role: Vice President of the United States
description: A former U.S. senator from Ohio and author of 'Hillbilly Elegy' who converted to Catholicism in 2019, Vance champions protectionist tariffs, mass deportation, cutting military aid to Ukraine, and pro-family natalist policies.

name: Marco Rubio
description: A Cuban American, former U.S. senator from Florida, and Secretary of State since 2025, he led the crackdown on Venezuela (capturing Maduro) and Cuba, champions tariffs and 'common good capitalism', and is a practicing Catholic opposed to abortion and same-sex marriage.

name: Nicolás Maduro
description: Hugo Chávez's successor, Maduro ruled Venezuela for 13 years deepening Chavista authoritarianism, with electoral fraud in 2024, repression by armed colectivos, and military alliances with Russia, China, and Iran, until his capture by the U.S. in 2026.

name: Pedro Sánchez
description: Secretary-general of the PSOE and Prime Minister of Spain since 2018, Sánchez governs in coalition with the left and support from Catalan pro-independence parties, championing historical memory, abortion, euthanasia and mass migrant regularization, while refusing to raise military spending to NATO's 5% GDP target.

name: Charles de Gaulle
description: President of France (1959–1969) and leader of the Resistance in World War II, de Gaulle founded the Fifth Republic with a strong presidency, withdrew France from NATO's integrated military command, and built an independent nuclear arsenal to secure strategic autonomy free of subordinate alliances.

name: Rudolf Rocker
description: German theorist of anarcho-syndicalism, Rocker championed revolutionary unions and free federations of communes in place of the state, and in Nationalism and Culture attacked nationalism and centralized power as enemies of cultural creation.

name: Errico Malatesta
description: Italian anarchist communist, Malatesta spent decades underground and in exile organizing insurrections and workers' newspapers, advocating the abolition of the state and private property through direct action while rejecting both parliamentarism and Bolshevik dictatorship.

name: Sidney Webb
description: Co-founder of the Fabian Society and the London School of Economics, Webb advocated a gradual parliamentary and administrative transition to socialism, drafted Clause IV of the British Labour Party, and praised Soviet planning in his old age.

name: Alberto Fujimori
description: President of Peru (1990–2000), Fujimori defeated the Shining Path insurgency and curbed hyperinflation through neoliberal shock therapy, but shut down Congress in the 1992 self-coup and was convicted of crimes against humanity and corruption.

name: Saddam Hussein
description: Dictator of Iraq for over two decades, Saddam Hussein led the Baath Party, fought the Iran-Iraq War and the Gulf War after invading Kuwait, violently repressed Kurds and Shiites, and was overthrown by the US-led invasion in 2003 and executed in 2006.

name: Richard Nixon
description: US President (1969–1974), Nixon opened relations with China, ended the dollar’s convertibility to gold, created the EPA and the war on drugs, and resigned after the Watergate scandal.

name: Charles III
description: King of the United Kingdom since 2022, Charles III combines constitutional neutrality with decades of environmental activism and advocacy for organic farming, traditional urbanism and interfaith dialogue, having lobbied ministers in the “black spider memos” and acknowledged the Empire’s slaving past.

name: Vitalik Buterin
description: Creator of Ethereum, Buterin formulated d/acc — defensive, decentralized technological acceleration —, funds public goods through quadratic funding, champions cryptography and privacy, condemned Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and criticizes both the state and corporate monopolies.

name: Howard Scott
description: American engineer, Scott founded Technocracy Incorporated in 1933, proposing to replace the price system and money with energy certificates and to hand the government of a continental “technate” to engineers and scientists instead of politicians and businessmen.

name: James Lovelock
description: British independent scientist, Lovelock formulated the Gaia hypothesis, which sees Earth as a self-regulating system, warned about global warming, broke with environmentalism by defending nuclear power and predicted in “Novacene” that cyborgs would succeed humanity.

name: Benjamin Constant
description: Franco-Swiss theorist of liberalism, Constant distinguished the liberty of the ancients from that of the moderns, denounced unlimited popular sovereignty as the origin of the Terror, and defended individual rights, a free press and constitutional monarchy with a property-based franchise.

name: Martin Luther King Jr.
description: Baptist minister and leader of the American civil rights movement, King led the Montgomery bus boycott and the March on Washington, advocating nonviolent civil disobedience, an end to racial segregation, economic redistribution and opposition to the Vietnam War.

name: Carl Gustaf Emil Mannerheim
description: Commander of Finnish forces and later president, Mannerheim led the defense against the Soviet invasion in the Winter War, sustaining universal conscription and fortifications, yet refusing to advance on Leningrad and seeking a separate peace in 1944.
